#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/integration/orch-timeout-applies-test.sh
#
# SPEC-1 (#1801): A hung work unit dispatched through the fanout, map, or
# sequential strategy stops at its stage template `timeout_s:` limit; the
# 300 s flat deadline no longer applies.
#
# Old code: every strategy calls
#   orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "${ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300}"
# New code: every strategy calls
#   orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")"
#
# This test fails on old code (spy captures 300), passes on new code
# (spy captures the template's timeout_s: value).
#
# [#1801/SPEC-1]
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
# template.sh also sources scripts/lib/stage-time-limit.sh
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"

print_test_header "orch strategies pass template timeout_s: (not 300s) to orch_collect (#1801 SPEC-1)"
setup_test_env "orch-timeout-applies"

# ── Template with timeout_s: 7 for stage "testjob" ──────────────────────────
# The spy test asserts orch_collect receives --timeout 7, NOT --timeout 300.
TPL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/tpl-spec1.yaml"
cat > "$TPL" <<'YAML'
id: tpl-spec1
name: spec1 test
defaults:
  strategy: fanout
flow:
  - testjob
testjob:
  roles: [testworker]
  timeout_s: 7
YAML
load_template "$TPL" >/dev/null 2>&1

# Source the strategies (after template.sh so _TPL_SOURCE_FILE is set)
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh"

# ── Minimal plugin for resolve_plugin_for_role ───────────────────────────────
_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins/agent/testworker"
mkdir -p "$_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR"
cat > "$_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR/manifest.yaml" <<'MF'
id: testworker
name: testworker
kind: agent
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: testworker_run
provides:
  role: testworker
MF
cat > "$_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh" <<'PL'
testworker_run() { return 0; }
PL

# Mock orch functions, platform detection, and plugin resolution so the
# strategy machinery runs without a real backend or runner environment.
_DETECTED_PLATFORMS=("generic")
resolve_plugin_for_role() { printf '%s\n' "$_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR"; return 0; }

_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
_SPEC1_OC_CALLS=0
orch_collect() {
    _SPEC1_OC_CALLS=$(( _SPEC1_OC_CALLS + 1 ))
    _SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
    local _s1_pool="$1"; shift
    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            --timeout) _SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
            *) shift ;;
        esac
    done
    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
    return 0
}
orch_spawn()    { return 0; }
orch_dispatch() { printf 'slot-%s\n' "$$"; return 0; }
orch_shutdown() { return 0; }

export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
printf '{"schema_version":1}' > "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
export ZBUILD_RUN_ID="spec1-test"
export ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/orch-scratch"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH"
export ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE="testjob"

_spec1_expected_timeout="$(template_stage_time_limit testjob)"

# ── SPEC-1a: fanout passes template timeout_s: (not 300) to orch_collect ─────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] fanout strategy uses template_stage_time_limit for orch_collect"
unset ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT 2>/dev/null || true
_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/integration/orch-backend-misconfigured-test.sh
#
# SPEC-2 (#1801): Running with a backend configured as `sequential` (or any
# name that resolves to no plugin) fails the run as `misconfigured` naming the
# backend; the sequential fallback in `orch_load_backend` is removed.
#
# SPEC-4 (#1801): A configured backend plugin that is absent from the installed
# tree (not the checkout) fails the run as `misconfigured` naming the missing
# backend.
#
# SPEC-10 (#1801): A backend whose plugin directory is present but whose config
# file is unreadable (permissions, corrupt, or missing) fails the run as
# `misconfigured` naming the backend — tested from the installed tree.
#
# All three must FAIL on old code (which has the sequential fallback) and PASS
# on new code (which removes the fallback and returns 1 naming the backend).
#
# Old code behaviour under each SPEC:
#   SPEC-2: orch_load_backend "sequential" → hardcoded path to the fallback backend
#           via hardcoded path → sources it → returns 0.
#   SPEC-4: orch_load_backend "absent-backend" → _orch_find_backend_dir fails →
#           general sequential fallback fires → returns 0 with a warning.
#   SPEC-10: source on unreadable plugin.sh fails silently (no set -e in contract.sh) →
#            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1 runs anyway → returns 0.
#
# New code: every case returns 1, _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED stays 0, and
# stderr names the backend.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-2] [#1801/SPEC-4] [#1801/SPEC-10]
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "orch_load_backend fails misconfigured naming backend when fallback removed (#1801 SPEC-2,4,10)"
setup_test_env "orch-backend-misconfigured"

# Prevent auto-config-file reads from picking up the project's real config.
export ZBUILD_CONFIG_FILE="/dev/null"
export ZBUILD_PROJECT_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/project"

# Source contract.sh — it auto-calls _orch_load_backend at end.
# With ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT pointing at an empty dir and no zbuild_config_get_backend
# available, it defaults to "sequential" and:
#   old code: sources the fallback backend via hardcoded _ZBUILD_ROOT path → BACKEND_LOADED=1
#   new code: no fallback → orch_load_backend returns 1 (silenced by || true) → BACKEND_LOADED=0
# We reset _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0 before each SPEC section so the
# explicit call we are testing starts from a clean state.
_EMPTY_PLUGINS="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/empty-plugins"
mkdir -p "$_EMPTY_PLUGINS"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_EMPTY_PLUGINS"
export ZBUILD_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKEND="sequential"

# shellcheck source=../../core/orch/contract.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/contract.sh"

# ── SPEC-2: "sequential" name resolves to no plugin (fallback removed) ───────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] orch_load_backend 'sequential' fails when sequential fallback is removed"

_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_EMPTY_PLUGINS"
_SPEC2_ERR=""
_SPEC2_RC=0
_SPEC2_ERR="$(orch_load_backend "sequential" 2>&1)" || _SPEC2_RC=$?

if [[ "$_SPEC2_RC" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] orch_load_backend 'sequential' returns non-zero (sequential fallback removed)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] orch_load_backend 'sequential' must return non-zero (sequential fallback removed)" \
        "returned 0; old code finds the fallback backend via hardcoded _ZBUILD_ROOT path and sources it"
fi

if [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -ne 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is not 1 (backend correctly not loaded)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED must not be 1 when backend failed to load" \
        "sentinel set to 1; old code sets it after sourcing the hardcoded sequential path"
fi

if grep -q 'sequential' <<< "$_SPEC2_ERR"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] error output names the backend 'sequential'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] error output must name the backend 'sequential'" \
        "stderr did not contain 'sequential'; got: ${_SPEC2_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

# The run must be reported as `misconfigured` (not a generic failure).
# New code emits "misconfigured" in its error message or sets
# _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured; old code silently succeeds
# so this never reaches a misconfigured path at all.
if grep -q 'misconfigured' <<< "$_SPEC2_ERR" || \
   [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION:-}" == "misconfigured" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] backend failure is reported as 'misconfigured'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] backend failure must be reported as 'misconfigured'" \
        "neither error output nor _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION contained 'misconfigured'; got: ${_SPEC2_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

# ── SPEC-4: absent backend plugin fails naming the missing backend ─────────────
# Backend name that is not present in the empty ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT and has no
# hardcoded fallback. Old code falls back to sequential silently; new code fails.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-4] orch_load_backend absent plugin fails naming backend (no general fallback)"

_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_EMPTY_PLUGINS"
_SPEC4_ERR=""
_SPEC4_RC=0
_SPEC4_ERR="$(orch_load_backend "orch-absent-spec4" 2>&1)" || _SPEC4_RC=$?

if [[ "$_SPEC4_RC" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] orch_load_backend absent plugin returns non-zero (no fallback)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] orch_load_backend absent plugin must return non-zero (no fallback)" \
        "returned 0; old code's general sequential fallback fires for any missing backend"
fi

if [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -ne 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is not 1 (absent backend)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED must not be 1 for absent backend" \
        "sentinel set to 1; old code's general fallback to sequential sets it"
fi

if grep -q 'orch-absent-spec4' <<< "$_SPEC4_ERR"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] error output names the missing backend 'orch-absent-spec4'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] error output must name the missing backend 'orch-absent-spec4'" \
        "stderr: ${_SPEC4_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

if grep -q 'misconfigured' <<< "$_SPEC4_ERR" || \
   [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION:-}" == "misconfigured" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] absent backend failure is reported as 'misconfigured'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] absent backend failure must be reported as 'misconfigured'" \
        "neither error output nor _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION contained 'misconfigured'; got: ${_SPEC4_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

# ── SPEC-10: present dir, unreadable plugin.sh — fails naming the backend ─────
# Plugin directory and manifest are present (discovery succeeds) but plugin.sh
# is unreadable (chmod 000), simulating a corrupt or permission-denied install.
#
# Old code: source on unreadable file fails silently (no set -e in contract.sh),
#   then sets _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1 and returns 0.
# New code: detects source failure, returns 1 naming the backend.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] orch_load_backend unreadable plugin.sh fails naming backend"

_S10_PLUGINS="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec10-plugins"
_S10_PLUGIN_DIR="$_S10_PLUGINS/tool/orch-broken-spec10"
mkdir -p "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR"
cat > "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR/manifest.yaml" <<'MANIFEST'
id: orch-broken-spec10
name: Broken Backend Spec10
kind: tool
version: 0.0.1
provides:
  role: orchestrator-backend
  alias: orch-broken-spec10
MANIFEST
# Write a syntactically valid plugin.sh then remove read permission.
printf 'orch_spawn() { return 0; }\norch_capabilities() { printf '"'"'{}'"'"'; }\n' \
    > "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh"
chmod 000 "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh"

export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_S10_PLUGINS"
_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
_SPEC10_ERR=""
_SPEC10_RC=0
_SPEC10_ERR="$(orch_load_backend "orch-broken-spec10" 2>&1)" || _SPEC10_RC=$?

# Restore permissions so cleanup_test_env can remove the directory.
chmod 644 "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh" 2>/dev/null || true

if [[ "$_SPEC10_RC" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] orch_load_backend with unreadable plugin.sh returns non-zero"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] orch_load_backend with unreadable plugin.sh must return non-zero" \
        "returned 0; old code: source fails silently, _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1 runs anyway, returns 0"
fi

if [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -ne 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is not 1 (unreadable plugin.sh)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED must not be 1 when plugin.sh unreadable" \
        "sentinel set to 1; old code sets it even when source fails"
fi

if grep -q 'orch-broken-spec10' <<< "$_SPEC10_ERR"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] error output names the backend 'orch-broken-spec10'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] error output must name the backend 'orch-broken-spec10'" \
        "stderr: ${_SPEC10_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

if grep -q 'misconfigured' <<< "$_SPEC10_ERR" || \
   [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION:-}" == "misconfigured" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] unreadable plugin.sh failure is reported as 'misconfigured'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] unreadable plugin.sh failure must be reported as 'misconfigured'" \
        "neither error output nor _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION contained 'misconfigured'; got: ${_SPEC10_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Integration: #1831 — an `always_run:` stage runs on EVERY exit path.
3	#
4	# This is the assertion the attribute exists for. A mechanism that fires on four
5	# of five exit paths is #1878's defect wearing a new name ("the snapshot was
6	# never called"), so each path gets its own case and names itself on failure —
7	# a single parameterised assertion would report "one of five" and leave the
8	# operator to find which.
9	#
10	# Paths covered: rc=0, rc=1, a stage killed by SIGINT (rc=130 + the recorded
11	# abort word), SIGTERM to the runner, and a release hook that hangs past its
12	# own timeout_s.
13	set -euo pipefail
14	
15	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
16	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
17	RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
18	
19	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
20	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
21	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
22	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
23	
24	print_test_header "always_run dispatches on every exit path (#1831)"
25	setup_test_env "zb-always-run-exit"
26	export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
27	
28	PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
29	export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
30	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
31	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
32	export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
33	export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
34	export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
35	export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
36	mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
37	printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"
38	
39	OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo always-run-overlay)"
40	install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" always-run-minimal
41	
42	# The always-run plugin, bound by ROLE (not by directory — that coupling is
43	# what #1831 removes). It touches a marker so "did it run?" is a file test
44	# rather than an inference from an event that might not be emitted.
45	mock_plugin_factory "outcome"  "agent" 0 "" ""         >/dev/null
46	mock_plugin_factory "teardown" "tool"  0 "" "teardown" >/dev/null
47	
48	RELEASE_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-ran"
49	RELEASE_ENTERED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-entered"
50	_arm_release() {
51	    # Two markers, not one. ENTERED is written before the optional sleep,
52	    # RAN after it. With a single completion marker, "the watchdog killed a
53	    # hanging hook" and "the hook was never dispatched at all" are the same
54	    # observation — and SPEC-5 passed for that wrong reason during development,
55	    # before the dispatch worked at all.
56	    # $1 = optional `sleep N` injected between the two, for the watchdog case.
57	    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
58	teardown_run() {
59	    : > "${RELEASE_ENTERED}"
60	    ${1:-:}
61	    : > "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
62	    return 0
63	}
64	PLUG
65	}
66	
67	# The stage announces that it is RUNNING (#2029). `pipeline-state.json` appears
68	# during startup, long before any stage is dispatched, so waiting on it and then
69	# sleeping a second is not "the stage has started" — it is a guess that happens to
70	# hold on an idle machine.
71	#
72	# On a loaded one it does not, and SPEC-4 then SIGTERMs a runner still setting up
73	# its worktree: no stage has run, no release hook is armed, no marker is written,
74	# and the assertion reports a missing file with no hint that the run never got
75	# that far. Observed directly — `wait` returned in 0s, the hook-entered marker was
76	# absent, and the runner's last line was "Working in the run's worktree".
77	#
78	# `runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh` already does this correctly with
79	# BUILD_STARTED; this is the same idea. The marker can only appear once the stage
80	# is genuinely executing, so load can only delay it, never fake it.
81	# #1850: the stage writes the v2 result its manifest (mock_plugin_factory's)
82	# promises — pass on rc 0, error/broken otherwise — so a run that should succeed
83	# is not failed for leaving no readable result.
84	_arm_outcome() {
85	    local _o=pass
86	    [[ "${2:-0}" -ne 0 ]] && _o=broken
87	    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/outcome/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
88	outcome_run() {
89	    : > "\${STAGE_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
90	    ${1:-:}
91	    $(mock_result_line outcome "$_o")
92	    return ${2:-0}
93	}
94	PLUG
95	}
96	
97	# Each case gets its own state dir: a stale marker or state file from a prior
98	# case would make a later one pass for the wrong reason.
99	_run_case() {
100	    local name="$1" rc_want_set="$2"
101	    rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
102	    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-$name"
103	    mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
104	    set +e
105	    ( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
106	        --goal "always-run $name" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/$name.out" 2>&1
107	    _CASE_RC=$?
108	    set -e
109	    [[ "$rc_want_set" == "skip" ]] || true
110	}
111	
112	# ─── [SPEC-1][change] rc=0 — the ordinary success path ──────────────────────
113	print_test_section "[SPEC-1][change] release runs when the pipeline succeeds"
114	_arm_release; _arm_outcome "" 0
115	_run_case "rc0" skip
116	assert_file_exists "[SPEC-1] release ran on rc=0" "$RELEASE_MARKER"
117	
118	# ─── [SPEC-2][change] rc=1 — a failed run still frees its resources ─────────
119	# The failing path is the one that matters most: a run that died is exactly the
120	# run holding process groups and locks nobody else will clean up.
121	print_test_section "[SPEC-2][change] release runs when a stage fails"
122	_arm_release; _arm_outcome "" 1
123	_run_case "rc1" skip
124	assert_file_exists "[SPEC-2] release ran on a non-zero stage rc" "$RELEASE_MARKER"
125	
126	# ─── [SPEC-3][change] the SIGINT path ─────────────────────────────────────
127	# #1850 (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025): the SIGINT path is the recorded abort word, not
128	# rc=130 — a bare 130 from a stage is just a failed stage now. So the stage
129	# does what a Ctrl-C does to the process group: the sentinel is armed (empty =
130	# sigint) and the child dies with 130. The run must end on the abort path —
131	# exit 1, status interrupted — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2.
132	print_test_section "[SPEC-3][change] release runs on the SIGINT path (abort word sigint)"
133	_arm_release
134	# shellcheck disable=SC2016  # expanded by the stage at run time, not here
135	_arm_outcome ': > "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/.abort.signal"' 130
136	_run_case "rc130" skip
137	assert_file_exists "[SPEC-3] release ran on the SIGINT path" "$RELEASE_MARKER"
138	assert_eq "[SPEC-3] the run took the abort path: exit 1 (not 130), status interrupted" \
139	    "1 interrupted" "$_CASE_RC $(jq -r '.status // "MISSING"' "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-rc130/pipeline-state.json" 2>/dev/null)"
140	
141	# ─── [SPEC-4][change] SIGTERM delivered to the runner itself ───────────────
142	# Distinct from SPEC-3: there the stage returned a code, here the signal is
143	# delivered to the runner process while a stage is still executing. #1759's
144	# re-armed INT/TERM traps are what give this path somewhere to hang off.
145	print_test_section "[SPEC-4][change] release runs when the runner is SIGTERMed mid-stage"
146	_arm_release; _arm_outcome "sleep 30" 0
147	rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
148	export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-sigterm"
149	export STAGE_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-started-sigterm"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration: #1831 — an `always_run:` stage runs on EVERY exit path.
#
# This is the assertion the attribute exists for. A mechanism that fires on four
# of five exit paths is #1878's defect wearing a new name ("the snapshot was
# never called"), so each path gets its own case and names itself on failure —
# a single parameterised assertion would report "one of five" and leave the
# operator to find which.
#
# Paths covered: rc=0, rc=1, a stage killed by SIGINT (rc=130 + the recorded
# abort word), SIGTERM to the runner, and a release hook that hangs past its
# own timeout_s.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "always_run dispatches on every exit path (#1831)"
setup_test_env "zb-always-run-exit"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo always-run-overlay)"
install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" always-run-minimal

# The always-run plugin, bound by ROLE (not by directory — that coupling is
# what #1831 removes). It touches a marker so "did it run?" is a file test
# rather than an inference from an event that might not be emitted.
mock_plugin_factory "outcome"  "agent" 0 "" ""         >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "teardown" "tool"  0 "" "teardown" >/dev/null

RELEASE_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-ran"
RELEASE_ENTERED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-entered"
_arm_release() {
    # Two markers, not one. ENTERED is written before the optional sleep,
    # RAN after it. With a single completion marker, "the watchdog killed a
    # hanging hook" and "the hook was never dispatched at all" are the same
    # observation — and SPEC-5 passed for that wrong reason during development,
    # before the dispatch worked at all.
    # $1 = optional `sleep N` injected between the two, for the watchdog case.
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
teardown_run() {
    : > "${RELEASE_ENTERED}"
    ${1:-:}
    : > "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    return 0
}
PLUG
}

# The stage announces that it is RUNNING (#2029). `pipeline-state.json` appears
# during startup, long before any stage is dispatched, so waiting on it and then
# sleeping a second is not "the stage has started" — it is a guess that happens to
# hold on an idle machine.
#
# On a loaded one it does not, and SPEC-4 then SIGTERMs a runner still setting up
# its worktree: no stage has run, no release hook is armed, no marker is written,
# and the assertion reports a missing file with no hint that the run never got
# that far. Observed directly — `wait` returned in 0s, the hook-entered marker was
# absent, and the runner's last line was "Working in the run's worktree".
#
# `runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh` already does this correctly with
# BUILD_STARTED; this is the same idea. The marker can only appear once the stage
# is genuinely executing, so load can only delay it, never fake it.
# #1850: the stage writes the v2 result its manifest (mock_plugin_factory's)
# promises — pass on rc 0, error/broken otherwise — so a run that should succeed
# is not failed for leaving no readable result.
_arm_outcome() {
    local _o=pass
    [[ "${2:-0}" -ne 0 ]] && _o=broken
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/outcome/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
outcome_run() {
    : > "\${STAGE_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
    ${1:-:}
    $(mock_result_line outcome "$_o")
    return ${2:-0}
}
PLUG
}

# Each case gets its own state dir: a stale marker or state file from a prior
# case would make a later one pass for the wrong reason.
_run_case() {
    local name="$1" rc_want_set="$2"
    rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-$name"
    mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
    set +e
    ( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
        --goal "always-run $name" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/$name.out" 2>&1
    _CASE_RC=$?
    set -e
    [[ "$rc_want_set" == "skip" ]] || true
}

# ─── [SPEC-1][change] rc=0 — the ordinary success path ──────────────────────
print_test_section "[SPEC-1][change] release runs when the pipeline succeeds"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "" 0
_run_case "rc0" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-1] release ran on rc=0" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-2][change] rc=1 — a failed run still frees its resources ─────────
# The failing path is the one that matters most: a run that died is exactly the
# run holding process groups and locks nobody else will clean up.
print_test_section "[SPEC-2][change] release runs when a stage fails"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "" 1
_run_case "rc1" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-2] release ran on a non-zero stage rc" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-3][change] the SIGINT path ─────────────────────────────────────
# #1850 (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025): the SIGINT path is the recorded abort word, not
# rc=130 — a bare 130 from a stage is just a failed stage now. So the stage
# does what a Ctrl-C does to the process group: the sentinel is armed (empty =
# sigint) and the child dies with 130. The run must end on the abort path —
# exit 1, status interrupted — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2.
print_test_section "[SPEC-3][change] release runs on the SIGINT path (abort word sigint)"
_arm_release
# shellcheck disable=SC2016  # expanded by the stage at run time, not here
_arm_outcome ': > "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/.abort.signal"' 130
_run_case "rc130" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-3] release ran on the SIGINT path" "$RELEASE_MARKER"
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] the run took the abort path: exit 1 (not 130), status interrupted" \
    "1 interrupted" "$_CASE_RC $(jq -r '.status // "MISSING"' "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-rc130/pipeline-state.json" 2>/dev/null)"

# ─── [SPEC-4][change] SIGTERM delivered to the runner itself ───────────────
# Distinct from SPEC-3: there the stage returned a code, here the signal is
# delivered to the runner process while a stage is still executing. #1759's
# re-armed INT/TERM traps are what give this path somewhere to hang off.
print_test_section "[SPEC-4][change] release runs when the runner is SIGTERMed mid-stage"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "sleep 30" 0
rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-sigterm"
export STAGE_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-started-sigterm"
rm -f "$STAGE_STARTED"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
    --goal "always-run sigterm" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/sigterm.out" 2>&1 &
_runner_pid=$!
# Wait for the run to actually reach the stage before signalling — signalling a
# runner still in startup would prove nothing about the exit path.
#
# #2029: this used to wait for `pipeline-state.json` and then sleep 1. That file
# is written during STARTUP, so the wait proved nothing and the sleep was the only
# real margin. Under load it was not enough and the signal landed mid-startup.
# STAGE_STARTED is written by the stage itself, so it cannot be reached early.
_waited=0
while [[ ! -f "$STAGE_STARTED" && $_waited -lt 300 ]]; do
    sleep 0.2; _waited=$(( _waited + 1 ))
done
if [[ ! -f "$STAGE_STARTED" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the stage started before the signal was sent" \
        "STAGE_STARTED never appeared in 60s — the run never reached a stage, so the exit path was never exercised"
fi
_spec4_t0=$(date +%s)
kill -TERM "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
_spec4_wait_s=$(( $(date +%s) - _spec4_t0 ))
# The trap runs in the dying process; give it a moment to land the marker.
_waited=0
while [[ ! -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" && $_waited -lt 50 ]]; do
    sleep 0.2; _waited=$(( _waited + 1 ))
done

# #2029: say WHAT WAS SEEN, not merely that the file is absent.
#
# This assertion has failed intermittently on CI for as long as it has existed,
# and it could never be diagnosed because "file not found" is the same output
# whether the runner ignored the signal, died before its trap, ran teardown into
# a different path, or simply had not finished yet. Three separate mechanisms
# were proposed for it and all three were disproven.
#
# The sibling assertion in runner-release-exit-paths prints the marker it read,
# and that one line is what let #2046 identify its cause in minutes after days of
# guessing. This is that lesson applied here: the next occurrence explains itself
# instead of starting another hunt.
if [[ ! -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" ]]; then
    {
        printf '  DIAGNOSTIC [SPEC-4]: release marker absent after %ss of polling\n' "$(( _waited * 2 / 10 ))"
        printf '    wait on the runner returned after: %ss\n' "$_spec4_wait_s"
        printf '    runner pid %s still alive: %s\n' "$_runner_pid" \
            "$(kill -0 "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null && echo YES || echo no)"
        printf '    release hook ENTERED marker: %s\n' \
            "$([[ -f "$RELEASE_ENTERED" ]] && echo present || echo absent)"
        printf '    state dir: %s\n' \
            "$([[ -d "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" ]] && (cd "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" && printf '%s ' * 2>/dev/null) || echo '<missing>')"
        printf '    runner output (last 5 lines):\n'
        tail -5 "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/sigterm.out" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/      /' || printf '      <no output>\n'
    } >&2
fi
# RELEASE_ENTERED separates "the hook never started" from "it started and did not
# finish" — the single most useful split, and the one the bare check cannot make.
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-4] release ran after SIGTERM to the runner" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-5][guard] a hanging release cannot hang the exit ────────────────
# The stage declares timeout_s: 2. A hook that blocks past it must be killed and
# the exit must continue — otherwise Ctrl-C becomes a lockup, which is the exact
# class of bug an EXIT-trap dispatch exists to avoid. Asserting the WALL CLOCK
# rather than the marker: the marker would also be absent if release never ran
# at all, so it cannot distinguish "bounded" from "broken".
print_test_section "[SPEC-5][guard] a release hook that hangs is bounded by its timeout_s"
_arm_release "sleep 60"; _arm_outcome "" 0
rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-hang"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
_t0=$(date +%s)
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
    --goal "always-run hang" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/hang.out" 2>&1
set -e
_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
# 45s is generous against a 2s bound plus runner startup; the assertion is
# "bounded at all", not a tight budget — a tight one would flake under a loaded
# parallel pool (the #991 lesson).
if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 45 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-5] a 60s release hook did not hold the exit (${_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-5] a 60s release hook held the exit" "elapsed=${_elapsed}s"
fi
# These two together are what make the case meaningful: the hook WAS entered
# (so the bound is what stopped it) and did NOT complete (so it was actually
# killed). Either alone is satisfied by a dispatch that never happened.
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-5] the hanging hook was actually dispatched" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
assert_file_not_exists "[SPEC-5] the hanging hook was killed before completing" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-6][guard] an unresolvable always-run role is LOUD ───────────────
# The code this replaces did `[[ -d "$_td_dir" ]] || return 0` — a missing
# plugin was a silent no-op. An always-run stage that cannot be resolved has not
# run, and the operator must be able to see that rather than infer it from a
# missing effect.
print_test_section "[SPEC-6][guard] an unresolvable role emits an event instead of failing silently"
_arm_outcome "" 0
rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER"
rm -rf "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-unresolved"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events/unresolved.jsonl"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
    --goal "always-run unresolved" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/unresolved.out" 2>&1
_unres_rc=$?
set -e
assert_event_emitted "[SPEC-6] stage.always_run.unresolved is emitted" \
    "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" "stage.always_run.unresolved"
# And it must not change the run's fate — an always-run stage never decides the
# verdict, including when it could not be found.
assert_eq "[SPEC-6] an unresolvable always-run stage does not fail the run" "0" "$_unres_rc"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
3	# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
4	# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
5	#
6	# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
7	# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
8	# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
9	#
10	# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
11	# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
12	# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
13	# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
14	# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
15	# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
16	# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
17	# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
18	# the process group would.
19	#
20	# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
21	# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
22	set -euo pipefail
23	
24	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
25	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
26	RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
27	
28	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
29	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
30	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
31	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
32	
33	print_test_header "runner dispatches cleanup(release) on every exit path (#1829)"
34	setup_test_env "runner-release-exit-paths"
35	export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
36	
37	PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
38	export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
39	export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
40	export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
41	export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
42	mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT"
43	
44	# The teardown plugin resolves its repo root by walking three levels up from
45	# its own directory (plugin-bootstrap), using a LOGICAL pwd — so symlinking the
46	# plugin itself would resolve to TEST_TEMP_DIR and fail to find helpers.sh.
47	# Give TEST_TEMP_DIR the shape of a repo root instead, then copy teardown in.
48	ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/scripts"
49	ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/core"    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/core"
50	mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool"
51	cp -R "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/teardown" "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"
52	
53	mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
54	mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
55	mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null
56	
57	# Declare the optional cleanup hook — without it plugin_hook_call emits
58	# `plugin.cleanup.absent`, returns 0 (#1823: rc is binary), and the stage is a
59	# no-op rather than a witness.
60	# Re-emit the manifest rather than appending: `cleanup:` has to sit inside the
61	# contiguous `hooks:` block, and mock_plugin_factory already wrote `requires:`
62	# after it. #1850/#2366: the re-emitted manifest keeps the factory's declaration —
63	# result_contract 3 and a JSON primary each run hook below writes.
64	for _spec in "agent/intake:intake:intake_cleanup" "agent/build:build:build_cleanup" "tool/test:test:test_cleanup"; do
65	    _dir="${_spec%%:*}"; _rest="${_spec#*:}"; _id="${_rest%%:*}"; _fn="${_rest#*:}"
66	    _kind="${_dir%%/*}"
67	    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/$_dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
68	id: $_id
69	name: Test $_id
70	kind: $_kind
71	version: 0.0.1
72	hooks:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
#
# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
# the process group would.
#
# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "runner dispatches cleanup(release) on every exit path (#1829)"
setup_test_env "runner-release-exit-paths"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT"

# The teardown plugin resolves its repo root by walking three levels up from
# its own directory (plugin-bootstrap), using a LOGICAL pwd — so symlinking the
# plugin itself would resolve to TEST_TEMP_DIR and fail to find helpers.sh.
# Give TEST_TEMP_DIR the shape of a repo root instead, then copy teardown in.
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/scripts"
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/core"    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/core"
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool"
cp -R "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/teardown" "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"

mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null

# Declare the optional cleanup hook — without it plugin_hook_call emits
# `plugin.cleanup.absent`, returns 0 (#1823: rc is binary), and the stage is a
# no-op rather than a witness.
# Re-emit the manifest rather than appending: `cleanup:` has to sit inside the
# contiguous `hooks:` block, and mock_plugin_factory already wrote `requires:`
# after it. #1850/#2366: the re-emitted manifest keeps the factory's declaration —
# result_contract 3 and a JSON primary each run hook below writes.
for _spec in "agent/intake:intake:intake_cleanup" "agent/build:build:build_cleanup" "tool/test:test:test_cleanup"; do
    _dir="${_spec%%:*}"; _rest="${_spec#*:}"; _id="${_rest%%:*}"; _fn="${_rest#*:}"
    _kind="${_dir%%/*}"
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/$_dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
id: $_id
name: Test $_id
kind: $_kind
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: ${_id//-/_}_run
  cleanup: $_fn
requires:
  core:
    - redaction
provides:

outputs:

    path: \${artifact_dir}/${_id}-result.json
    type: ${_id}-result.json@1
    format: json
    required: true
    primary: true
EOF
done

cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
intake_run() {
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/intake-result.json"
    return 0
}
intake_cleanup() { printf 'intake:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
PLUG

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# scripts/lib/lint-test-errexit.sh — #2252 G
     3	#
     4	# A test file that runs without stop-on-error (its first `set -…` line has no
     5	# `e`) must not turn it on later: from that line every assertion that expects a
     6	# non-zero rc kills the file instead of being checked. #1844's test-author
     7	# wrapped a call in `set +e … set -e` inside a `set -uo pipefail` file and the
     8	# next expected rc=1 aborted it. A file that starts with -e may toggle it.
     9	#
    10	# Usage: bash scripts/lib/lint-test-errexit.sh [root]   (default: the repo)
    11	# Exit:  0 = clean; 1 = at least one offending file.
    12	set -euo pipefail
    13	
    14	_LTE_ROOT="${1:-$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../.." && pwd)}"
    15	_bad=0
    16	while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    17	    [[ "$f" == */legacy-DoNotUse/* ]] && continue
    18	    # One awk pass: the header is the first `set -<flags>` line of the file's own
    19	    # shell; heredoc bodies are skipped — a fixture script written by the test is
    20	    # not the test's own shell (its `set -e` is the fixture's business).
    21	    while IFS=$'\t' read -r ln header; do
    22	        [[ -n "$ln" ]] || continue
    23	        echo "lint-test-errexit: ${f#"$_LTE_ROOT"/}:$ln turns stop-on-error on in a file that runs without it (header: ${header:-none}) — an expected non-zero rc after this line kills the file; use 'cmd || rc=\$?' instead" >&2
    24	        _bad=$((_bad + 1))
    25	    done < <(awk '
    26	        doc != "" { t = $0; sub(/^\t+/, "", t); if (t == doc) doc = ""; next }
    27	        /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
    28	        # The line itself is judged BEFORE a heredoc it opens hides what follows:
    29	        # a set -e on the opening line belongs to the test shell (review #2253).
    30	        !seen && /^set -[a-zA-Z]+/ {
    31	            seen = 1; hdr = $0; f = $2; sub(/^-/, "", f)
    32	            haserr = (f ~ /e/); next
    33	        }
    34	        seen && !haserr && /^[[:space:]]*set -[a-zA-Z]*e[a-zA-Z]*([[:space:]]|$)/ { print NR "\t" hdr }
    35	        {
    36	            line = $0
    37	            if (match(line, /<<-?[[:space:]]*["\047]?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*["\047]?/)) {
    38	                d = substr(line, RSTART, RLENGTH); sub(/^<<-?[[:space:]]*/, "", d); gsub(/["\047]/, "", d)
    39	                if (line !~ /<<</) doc = d
    40	            }
    41	        }
    42	    ' "$f" 2>/dev/null)
    43	done < <(find "$_LTE_ROOT/tests" "$_LTE_ROOT/plugins" -name '*-test.sh' -print0 2>/dev/null)
    44	
    45	if (( _bad > 0 )); then
    46	    echo "lint-test-errexit: $_bad file(s) switch stop-on-error on mid-file" >&2
    47	    exit 1
    48	fi
    49	echo "lint-test-errexit: clean"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh — parallel per-platform dispatch (issue #198/#222)
# ADR-009: all platforms run concurrently; stage succeeds iff all succeed (rc=2 = partial).
# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT}/common.sh"

# ─── _strategy_run_fanout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _strategy_run_fanout <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated (no orch_spawn called here)
#   stage      — stage name (e.g. "intake")
#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
#
# Dispatches one work unit per role×platform pair in parallel via orch_dispatch.
# Collects all results with orch_collect.
# Calls orch_shutdown and cleans up work units on both success and failure paths.
#
# Returns:
#   0 — all succeeded
#   1 — all failed (collect failure with no successes)
#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail); callers treat as stage fail
#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
_strategy_run_fanout() {
    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
    # | infra_failed | failed.
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false dispatch_count=0
    local -a work_units=() dispatched_plugins=()

    local role platform plugin_dir wu
    while IFS= read -r role; do
        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
            # Intentional fail-open: resolver returns "" when no match — skip silently.
            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
            any_plugin_found=true

            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
                warn "fanout: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            work_units+=("$wu")

            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
                warn "fanout: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            dispatch_count=$((dispatch_count + 1))
            dispatched_plugins+=("$plugin_dir")
        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
        return 1
    fi

    # Only collect if at least one dispatch succeeded; otherwise pool is empty
    # and orch_collect would return 0 (no results) — misreported as success.
    if [[ "$dispatch_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        local collect_rc=0
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
        orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")" || collect_rc=$?

        # orch_collect: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, partial/timed_out named on
        # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME (#1850 — it was rc 2).
        if [[ $collect_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
            # #1906: no artifact check here. Each work unit calls plugin_hook_call
            # (strategies/common.sh), so scan_plugin_outputs has already enforced
            # every declared output for every dispatched plugin.
        elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "timed_out" ]]; then
            local _fanout_limit; _fanout_limit="$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")"
            warn "fanout: stage '${stage}' timed out after ${_fanout_limit}s" || true
            _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
            orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
            _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="timed_out"
            return 1
        elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "partial" ]]; then
            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        else
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        fi
    fi

    _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true

    if   [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]];    then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"; return 0
    elif [[ $success_count -gt 0 ]]; then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="partial"; return 1
    else                                  _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"; return 1
    fi
}

# ─── _strategy_cleanup_work_units ────────────────────────────────────────────
_strategy_cleanup_work_units() {
    [[ $# -eq 0 ]] && return 0
    rm -f "$@" 2>/dev/null || true
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh — serialized per-platform dispatch (issue #200/#222)
# ADR-009: platforms run one at a time; always halts on the first collect failure.
# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_SEQUENTIAL_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_SEQUENTIAL_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_SEQ="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_SEQ}/common.sh"

# ─── _strategy_run_sequential ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _strategy_run_sequential <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated
#   stage      — stage name
#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
#
# Dispatches one work unit at a time via orch_dispatch + orch_collect.
# Halts on first failure (does not continue to next platform/role).
# Always calls orch_shutdown on exit (success or failure).
# Artifact enforcement happens per work unit inside plugin_hook_call (#1906).
#
# Returns:
#   0 — all succeeded
#   1 — any collect/dispatch failure
#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
_strategy_run_sequential() {
    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
    # | infra_failed | failed.
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
    local any_plugin_found=false

    local role platform plugin_dir wu prc
    while IFS= read -r role; do
        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
            any_plugin_found=true

            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
                warn "sequential: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
                return 1
            }

            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
                warn "sequential: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                rm -f "$wu" 2>/dev/null || true
                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
                return 1
            }

            prc=0
            orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")" || prc=$?
            rm -f "$wu" 2>/dev/null || true

            if [[ $prc -ne 0 ]]; then
                if [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "timed_out" ]]; then
                    local _seq_limit; _seq_limit="$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")"
                    warn "sequential: stage '${stage}' timed out after ${_seq_limit}s" || true
                    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
                    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="timed_out"
                else
                    warn "sequential: stage=$stage role=$role platform=$platform failed (rc=$prc)" || true
                    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
                fi
                return 1
            fi

        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
    $any_plugin_found || { _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"; return 1; }
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"
    return 0
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/common.sh — shared helpers for strategy modules (issue #222)
# ADR-009 (platform-aware modularity), ADR-011 (pluggable orch backend)
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_COMMON_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_COMMON_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
_ZBUILD_ROOT="${_ZBUILD_ROOT:-$(cd "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR}/../../.." && pwd)}"

# ─── _strategy_validate_stage ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Allowlist: non-empty, no path-traversal sequences, no shell metacharacters.
# exit 0: valid; exit 1: invalid (#1850, ADR-054 §4 — was 2; the warning names why).
_strategy_validate_stage() {
    local stage="$1"
    [[ -z "$stage" ]] && return 1
    # Strict allowlist — identical to platform: prevents ' injection in the
    # heredoc literal and path-traversal in scratch dir names.
    if [[ ! "$stage" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ ]]; then
        warn "strategy: invalid stage name: ${stage}" || true
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# ─── _strategy_validate_platform ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Allowlist: non-empty, ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$.
# exit 0: valid; exit 1: invalid.
_strategy_validate_platform() {
    local platform="$1"
    [[ -z "$platform" ]] && return 1
    if [[ ! "$platform" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ ]]; then
        warn "strategy: invalid platform name: ${platform}" || true
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# ─── _strategy_orch_scratch_dir ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# #898: resolve the orch scratch dir. Default → per-run isolation under
# ~/.zbuild/state/runs/<run_id>/orch (the orchestrator analog of #889 state
# isolation) so concurrent runs never share scratch. An explicit
# ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH overrides. ZBUILD_RUN_ID is exported by the runner before
# any stage dispatch (falls back to "default" only if somehow unset).
_strategy_orch_scratch_dir() {
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH:-}" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH"
    else
        printf '%s' "${ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT:-${HOME}/.zbuild/state}/runs/${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-default}/orch"
    fi
}

# ─── _strategy_make_work_unit <plugin_dir> <stage> <state_file> [<platform>] [<map_element>] [<map_dimension>] [<env_target>] [<unit_element>] ───
# Creates a self-contained executable shell script that calls plugin_hook_call.
# Validates stage and platform before baking into the script body.
# Prints the path of the temp file; caller is responsible for cleanup (rm -f).
# exit 0: success; exit 1: a validation failure or the temp file could not be
# created — the warning says which (#1850: validation was exit 2).
#
# map_element / map_dimension (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2): generic element identity
# for non-platform map dimensions. When set, exports to the work unit:
#   ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT=<element>    — the current element (e.g. "security")
#   ZBUILD_MAP_DIMENSION=<dim>      — the dimension name (e.g. "lenses")
# Plugins read ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT to derive per-element identity when
# ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE is the group id, not an element-specific stage id.
#
# env_target (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2): an optional caller-named env var, set to
# the map element in the work unit — a generic dimension→env mapping declared by
# the template's `as:` field (e.g. lenses → ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID). Keeps existing
# plugins that read their own env var working unchanged; the var name lives in the
# template, never hardcoded here. Validated as a shell identifier before baking.
_strategy_make_work_unit() {
    local plugin_dir="$1" stage="$2" state_file="$3" platform="${4:-generic}"
    local map_element="${5:-}" map_dimension="${6:-}" env_target="${7:-}" unit_element="${8:-}"

    _strategy_validate_stage "$stage"   || return 1
    _strategy_validate_platform "$platform" || return 1
    [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && { warn "strategy: _strategy_make_work_unit: empty plugin_dir" || true; return 1; }
    # #1295 Copilot: map_element/map_dimension are baked as single-quoted literals
    # into the work-unit script — a value with ', whitespace, or a newline would
    # break out of the quotes (shell-injection). Fail closed with an actionable
    # error. Element allows '-' (matches stage/platform); dimension is a shell-safe
    # token used to name a bash array (_MAP_DIM_<dim>), so no '-'.
    if [[ -n "$map_element" && ! "$map_element" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ ]]; then
        warn "strategy: invalid map element: ${map_element} (expected ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$)" || true
        return 1
    fi
    # #1312 (minor): map_element set but map_dimension empty → ambiguous work-unit
    # identity (ZBUILD_MAP_DIMENSION would be '' in the baked script). Fail closed.
    if [[ -n "$map_element" && -z "$map_dimension" ]]; then
        warn "strategy: map_element set but map_dimension is empty — dimension required" || true
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ -n "$map_dimension" && ! "$map_dimension" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_]{1,64}$ ]]; then
        warn "strategy: invalid map dimension: ${map_dimension} (expected ^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,64}$)" || true
        return 1
    fi
    # unit_element (#1706): the caller's name for this member after the stage
    # (`<element>` or `<role>.<element>`); baked like the others, so validated.
    if [[ -n "$unit_element" && ! "$unit_element" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}(\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64})?$ ]]; then
        warn "strategy: invalid unit element: ${unit_element}" || true
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ -n "$env_target" && ! "$env_target" =~ ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,63}$ ]]; then
        warn "strategy: invalid env_target var name: ${env_target}" || true
        return 1
    fi

    local scratch_dir; scratch_dir="$(_strategy_orch_scratch_dir)"
    mkdir -p "$scratch_dir" 2>/dev/null && chmod 700 "$scratch_dir" 2>/dev/null || {
        warn "strategy: cannot create orch scratch dir: ${scratch_dir}" || true
        return 1
    }

    local wu
    # Note: no .sh suffix — macOS mktemp does not randomize names when a suffix follows XXXXXX.
    wu="$(mktemp "${scratch_dir}/wu-XXXXXX")" || {
        warn "strategy: mktemp failed for work unit" || true
        return 1
    }

    # Bake in fully-qualified, immutable paths at construction time.
    # Values are embedded as single-quoted literals to prevent re-expansion.
    # event-bus.sh is sourced so plugin_hook_call emits events to the shared
    # ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL (inherited env var from runner).
    #
    # Issue #307: ADR-009 §"ZBUILD_PLATFORM env contract" promises plugins
    # see ZBUILD_PLATFORM=<single-platform> per per-platform invocation.
    # ADR-001's hook-context table lists the older name ZBUILD_TARGET_PLATFORM
    # for the same value. We export both so plugins can rely on either; the
    # canonical name going forward is ZBUILD_PLATFORM (ADR-009 §6).
    local _map_env_lines=""
    if [[ -n "$map_element" ]]; then
        _map_env_lines="export ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT='${map_element}'
export ZBUILD_MAP_DIMENSION='${map_dimension}'"
        # env_target: template-named var also carrying the element (generic
        # dimension→env mapping). var name validated above; element is a bare
        # dimension token, single-quoted like the others.
        if [[ -n "$env_target" ]]; then
            _map_env_lines="${_map_env_lines}
export ${env_target}='${map_element}'"
        fi
    fi

    # #1706 (ADR-054 §3.1): the member's own name is <stage>.<element> — the
    # declared element, or the platform when the map is over platforms.
    # plugin_hook_call turns it into ZBUILD_UNIT for exactly one dispatch.
    local _unit_elem="${unit_element:-$map_element}"
    [[ -z "$_unit_elem" && "$platform" != "generic" ]] && _unit_elem="$platform"
    [[ -n "$_unit_elem" ]] && _map_env_lines="${_map_env_lines:+${_map_env_lines}
}export ZBUILD_UNIT_ELEMENT='${_unit_elem}'"

    cat > "$wu" <<WORKUNIT
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
source '${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/scripts/lib/helpers.sh'
source '${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/core/event-bus/event-bus.sh'
source '${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/core/plugin-registry/registry.sh'
export ZBUILD_PLATFORM='${platform}'
export ZBUILD_TARGET_PLATFORM='${platform}'
export ZBUILD_ROOT='${_ZBUILD_ROOT}'
${_map_env_lines}
plugin_hook_call '${plugin_dir}' run '${stage}' '${state_file}'
WORKUNIT

    chmod 700 "$wu"
    printf '%s\n' "$wu"
    return 0
}

if   command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=gtimeout
elif command -v timeout  >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=timeout
fi
if [[ -z "$_tbin" ]]; then
    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: [SPEC-5] external hard kill (no timeout binary available)" >&2
else
    # [#1801/SPEC-5]: #2029: the force-kill grace is DERIVED from the engine's own
    # teardown budget, not guessed.
    #
    # After #1801 the engine bounds each always-run stage by template_stage_time_limit
    # (top-level `timeout_s:` in the stage block), NOT by router.timeout_s or
    # ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT. The template below pins timeout_s: _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT
    # for release so the worst case is knowable and the grace derives from it.
    # This case relies on its hooks returning promptly rather than on the bound —
    # the grace is purely a safety net so a runner that ignores TERM cannot hang the
    # suite. Three stages release on this path, so an unpinned run could spend far
    # longer tidying up than the 3s literal that used to sit here.
    _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT=3
    _SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=$(( _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT * 3 + 6 ))   # 3 stages + margin
    # Create a repo with a template that has timeout_s: _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT for
    # release (top-level, read by template_stage_time_limit after #1801).
    _spec5_repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "release-exit-paths-spec5")"
    install_template_overlay "$_spec5_repo" resume-minimal
    if [[ -d "$_spec5_repo/.git/info" ]] && \
       ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_spec5_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
        printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_spec5_repo/.git/info/exclude"
    fi
    cat > "$_spec5_repo/.zbuild/templates/resume-timeout-bounded.yaml" <<YAMLEOF
id: resume-timeout-bounded
extends: resume-minimal
release:
  timeout_s: ${_SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT}
YAMLEOF
    set -m
    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec "$4" 120 bash "$2" --template resume-timeout-bounded --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$_spec5_repo" "$RUNNER" "release-timeout" "$_tbin" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
    set +m
    for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -s "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
    kill -TERM -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    ( sleep "$_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE"; kill -KILL -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true ) &
    _spec5_killer=$!
    wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    kill "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
    _assert_released "SPEC-5" intake build
fi

# ── SPEC-6: a blocking cleanup hook cannot hold the exit open ────────────────
# The dispatch runs inside the EXIT trap, so an unbounded hook would turn a
# normal exit into a hang — the same class of bug (a process that outlives the
# run) that this mechanism exists to prevent.
print_test_section "SPEC-6: a cleanup hook that blocks cannot hang the runner"
wait "$_SPEC6_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
CASE_DIR="$_SPEC6_DIR"
_elapsed="$(cat "$CASE_DIR/elapsed" 2>/dev/null || echo 999)"
# The blocking hook sleeps 120s. The bound is the release stage's own
# `timeout_s:` at the top-level stage block (read by template_stage_time_limit
# after #1801 — 30s in simple.yaml), so the runner returns in about 30s.
# Allow generous headroom for a loaded host while still failing an unbounded wait.
if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 60 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded (runner exited in ${_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded" "runner took ${_elapsed}s"
fi
# #2287: the bound must stop the hook, not just stop waiting for it. Before,
# the hook lived on after the run, finished its sleep ~2 min later, and wrote
# into a state folder the run no longer owned. The kills are sent before the
# runner returns; up to 1s covers the killed processes exiting on a loaded host.
_hook_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -n "$_hook_pid" ]]; then
    for _ in $(seq 1 10); do kill -0 "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done
fi
if [[ -z "$_hook_pid" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] fixture: the blocking hook recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook.pid"
elif kill -0 "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run" "pid $_hook_pid still alive after the runner returned"
    # Leave nothing behind for the rest of the suite: the hook first, so it
    # cannot carry on once its sleep ends, then the sleep it leaves orphaned.
    _hook_kids="$(pgrep -P "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    kill -KILL "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _k in $_hook_kids; do kill -KILL "$_k" 2>/dev/null || true; done
else
    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run"
fi

# ── SPEC-6b (#2333): a child that ignores TERM is killed too ────────────────
# The bound sends TERM to the hook's group, then KILL after a grace. The runner
# waited only for the group leader and cancelled the watchdog when it exited, so
# a member that ignored TERM never got the KILL and outlived the run.
print_test_section "SPEC-6b: a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
# The time bound itself is SPEC-6's check, on the same dispatch path; this
# case is only about what survives it.
wait "$_SPEC6B_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
CASE_DIR="$_SPEC6B_DIR"
_child_pid=""
for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
    _child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
done
_alive=1
# Only poll a pid that was recorded; a missing pid is reported as a fixture failure below.
if [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]]; then
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
fi
if [[ -z "$_child_pid" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] fixture: the child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid"
elif [[ "$_alive" -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run" "pid $_child_pid still alive 5s after the runner returned"
    kill -KILL "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
else
    assert_pass "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
fi

# ── [#1801/SPEC-5]: _runner_dispatch_always_run uses template_stage_time_limit ──
# A blocking hook under a template with `timeout_s: 5` for release (top-level)
# must stop in ~5s, NOT in ~30s (router.timeout_s: 30 inherited from simple).
# Old code reads _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_release (router.timeout_s = 30) and
# uses that as the watchdog → runner takes ~30s.
# New code reads template_stage_time_limit("release") = 5 → runner takes ~5s.
# Assertion at < 20s: FAILS on old code (~30s), PASSES on new code (~5s).
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-5]: always-run watchdog bound by timeout_s: (not router.timeout_s)"
wait "$_SPEC5_BOUND_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
CASE_DIR="$_SPEC5_BOUND_DIR"
_spec5_elapsed="$(cat "$CASE_DIR/elapsed" 2>/dev/null || echo 999)"
if [[ "$_spec5_elapsed" -lt 20 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run watchdog uses timeout_s: 5 (runner exited in ${_spec5_elapsed}s; would be ~30s with router.timeout_s)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run watchdog uses timeout_s: 5" \
        "runner took ${_spec5_elapsed}s — expected < 20s (timeout_s: 5); old code would use router.timeout_s: 30"
fi

# [#1801/SPEC-5] static guard: ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT must not appear in runner.sh.
# Old code reads ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT for the always-run watchdog; new code reads
# template_stage_time_limit instead. This grep fails on old code (the var is there)
# and passes on new code (it has been removed).
if ! grep -q 'ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT' "$RUNNER"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh does not reference ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT (removed in #1801)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh must not reference ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT" \
        "ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT still present in $RUNNER; must be replaced by template_stage_time_limit"
fi

# [#1801/SPEC-5] static guard: _runner_dispatch_always_run must not reference
# router.timeout_s (its bash manifestation: _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_*).
# Old code (runner.sh): local _ar_to_var="_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_${_ar_safe}"
# which reads router.timeout_s from the template config.
# New code: reads template_stage_time_limit instead.
# This grep fails on old code (the string is present) and passes on new (removed).
if ! grep -q '_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT' "$RUNNER"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh does not reference _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT (router.timeout_s removed from always-run watchdog in #1801)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh must not reference _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT (router.timeout_s)" \
        "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT still present in $RUNNER; must be replaced by template_stage_time_limit"
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

build_run() {
    printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" > "${BUILD_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
    if [[ "${BUILD_SLEEP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        local _i; for _i in $(seq 1 300); do sleep 0.1; done
    fi
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    [[ "${BUILD_ARM_ABORT:-0}" == "1" ]] && : > "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal"
    if [[ "${BUILD_RC:-0}" == "0" ]]; then
        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
    else
        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"broken","reason":"stub failure"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
    fi
    return "${BUILD_RC:-0}"
}
build_cleanup() {
    printf 'build:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    # A hook that never returns — used to prove the dispatch is bounded. It
    # records its own pid so SPEC-6 can check it does not outlive the run (#2287).
    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook.pid"
        sleep 120
    fi
    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        # #2333: a child that ignores TERM, under a hook shell that does not.
        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &
        wait
    fi
    return 0
}
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/test/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
test_run() {
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/test-result.json"
    return 0
}
test_cleanup() { printf 'test:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
PLUG

OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo release-exit-paths-repo)"
install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" resume-minimal
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

_case_no=0
# _prep <name> — fresh state dir + marker for one exit path.
_prep() {
    _case_no=$((_case_no + 1))
    CASE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-$_case_no-$1"
    mkdir -p "$CASE_DIR/state" "$CASE_DIR/events"
    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$CASE_DIR/state"
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$CASE_DIR/events"
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$CASE_DIR/events/events.jsonl"
    export RELEASE_MARKER="$CASE_DIR/release-marker"
    export BUILD_STARTED="$CASE_DIR/build-started"
    : > "$RELEASE_MARKER"
    unset BUILD_RC BUILD_SLEEP BUILD_ARM_ABORT 2>/dev/null || true
}

# _assert_released <case> <stage>... — EVERY named stage released, purge never.
#
# #1989: this used to grep the shared marker for any ':release' and pass. Three
# stages append to that one file, so one stage releasing masked two that never
# did — measured: neutering build_cleanup alone left the suite green, and it
# took neutering all three to turn it red. The assertion could only ever detect
# a TOTAL failure of the mechanism, never a partial one, which is the shape a
# real regression takes (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Each case now names the stages whose cleanup must have run. The sets differ
# by exit path because a stage only reaches release once it has been dispatched.
#
# ADR-062 §2: reclamation reads the process group recorded at DISPATCH, not the
# completion status map, so a stage killed mid-flight IS reclaimable. SPEC-4 and
# SPEC-5 therefore expect `build` as well as `intake` — build had demonstrably
# started (it wrote BUILD_STARTED) before the signal landed. Before #2001 both
# freed `intake` only, because teardown iterated `.stage_statuses`, which
# `_update_stage_status` writes only on complete/failed — i.e. after a stage
# returns, which a killed stage never does.
_assert_released() {
    local _case="$1"; shift
    local _marker; _marker="$(cat "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    local _stage _missing=""
    for _stage in "$@"; do
        grep -q "^${_stage}:release$" <<< "$_marker" || _missing="${_missing}${_stage} "
    done
    if [[ -z "$_missing" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*"
    else
        assert_fail "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*" \
            "no release from: ${_missing}| marker=$(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_marker")"
    fi
    if grep -q ':purge' <<< "$_marker"; then
        assert_fail "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run" "marker contained purge"
    else
        assert_pass "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run"
    fi
}

# SPEC-6 and SPEC-6b each wait out the release bound on purpose: their hook
# blocks, and the bound (the base template's release `timeout_s:` at the
# top-level stage block, 30s after #1801) is what ends it. Started here, each
# from its own repo, so that bound runs while SPEC-1..5 do; their assertions
# are made below, in order.
#
# SPEC-5 (#1801): a separate blocking run uses a template with timeout_s: 5
# for release (NOT router.timeout_s: 5) — old code reads router.timeout_s: 30
# and takes ~30s; new code reads template_stage_time_limit (timeout_s: 5) and
# exits in ~5s. Started here so it runs in parallel with SPEC-6/6b.
_start_blocking() {   # <case name> <hook switch> [template-id]
    local _repo; _repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "release-exit-paths-$1")"
    install_template_overlay "$_repo" resume-minimal
    local _tpl="${3:-resume-minimal}"
    (
        _prep "$1"
        export BUILD_RC=0 "$2"=1
        _t0=$(date +%s)
        ( cd "$_repo" && bash "$RUNNER" --template "$_tpl" --goal "release-$1" ) \
            >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 || true
        printf '%s\n' "$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))" > "$CASE_DIR/elapsed"
    ) &
}
_start_blocking blocking BLOCK_CLEANUP;                   _SPEC6_PID=$!
_start_blocking blocking-ignore-term BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM; _SPEC6B_PID=$!
_SPEC6_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-blocking"
_SPEC6B_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-blocking-ignore-term"

# [#1801/SPEC-5]: blocking run with timeout_s: 5 for release (top-level, read
# by template_stage_time_limit), while router.timeout_s: 30 is inherited from
# simple — distinguishes new code (uses timeout_s: 5) from old (router.timeout_s: 30).
_spec5_bound_repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "release-exit-paths-spec5-bound")"
install_template_overlay "$_spec5_bound_repo" resume-minimal
if [[ -d "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info" ]] && \
   ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
    printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info/exclude"
fi
cat > "$_spec5_bound_repo/.zbuild/templates/resume-spec5-bound.yaml" <<'YAML'
id: resume-spec5-bound
extends: resume-minimal
release:
  timeout_s: 5

# ── SPEC-4: external SIGTERM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-4: exit path = external SIGTERM"
_prep sigterm
export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1

    RUNNER_PID=$!

for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -s "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done

id: resume-minimal
name: Resume Minimal Pipeline
extends: simple
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

# Minimal 3-leaf roster (#1098, PC5): the resume-after-SIGINT contract
# (full-pipeline-sigint resume path, Wave 15-E #685) is NOT stage-count
# dependent — it needs only: a stage BEFORE build (intake) to prove resume
# skips an already-complete stage, the build stage that SIGINTs / re-runs,
# and a stage AFTER build (test) to prove resume continues past build.
# Replaces the full ~14-stage standard roster the test used to register so
# the two real subprocess runs (SIGINT + --resume) drive far fewer dispatch
# units. Linear flow, no cycles (resume logic is the same either way).
#
# #1270: this is a per-repo `.zbuild/templates/` overlay (extends: simple).
# When merged over the base, the resulting file carries BOTH the base `flow:`
# and this `stages:` list, so the loader treats it as OLD-shape and honors ONLY
# the stages below (the base roster is discarded — it just has to exist).
#
# Stages declare NO `roles:` block on purpose. With roles, the runner routes
# the stage through the fanout strategy (orch pool), which collapses a child
# rc=130 into a generic rc=1 — that would break the SIGINT-propagation

rc=$?
set -e
if [[ $rc -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "M2: all-fail returns 1 (got $rc) — not raw rc passthrough (pre-fix would have returned 5)"
else
    assert_fail "M2: all-fail returns 1" "got $rc (pre-fix would have returned 5, the first non-zero)"
fi
orch_shutdown "$pool"

# ─── M3: mixed → 2 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pool="m3-mixed"
orch_spawn "$pool" 3 ""
orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 1')" >/dev/null
orch_dispatch "$pool" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
set +e
orch_collect "$pool" >/dev/null
rc=$?
set -e
# #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc 1, and the partial-failure signal is the word.
assert_eq "M3: mixed returns 1" "1" "$rc"
assert_eq "M3: mixed is named partial" "partial" "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}"
orch_shutdown "$pool"

# ─── M4: empty pool → 0 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pool="m4-empty"
orch_spawn "$pool" 1 ""
set +e
orch_collect "$pool" >/dev/null
rc=$?
set -e
if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "M4: empty pool returns 0 (got $rc)"
else
    assert_fail "M4: empty pool returns 0" "got $rc"
fi
orch_shutdown "$pool"


# ─── M5 [#1801/SPEC-11]: pool isolation — two concurrent pools do not bleed ──
# Two pools are spawned independently and each dispatches its own work units.
# Collect on each pool must return only that pool's results: the passing pool
# returns 0 and the failing pool returns 1, with no cross-contamination.
# Fails if orch_collect drains a shared queue instead of a per-pool queue.
pool_pass="m5-pool-pass"
pool_fail="m5-pool-fail"
orch_spawn "$pool_pass" 2 ""
orch_spawn "$pool_fail" 2 ""

# Dispatch only passing work to pool_pass, only failing work to pool_fail.
orch_dispatch "$pool_pass" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
orch_dispatch "$pool_pass" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 0')" >/dev/null
orch_dispatch "$pool_fail" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 1')" >/dev/null
orch_dispatch "$pool_fail" "$(orch_work_unit 'exit 1')" >/dev/null

set +e
orch_collect "$pool_pass" >/dev/null
rc_pass=$?
orch_collect "$pool_fail" >/dev/null
rc_fail=$?
set -e

if [[ $rc_pass -eq 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] pool isolation: passing pool collect returns 0 (not contaminated by failing pool)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] pool isolation: passing pool collect must return 0" \
        "got $rc_pass — results from the failing pool may have bled into the passing pool"
fi
if [[ $rc_fail -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-11] pool isolation: failing pool collect returns 1 (not contaminated by passing pool)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-11] pool isolation: failing pool collect must return 1" \
        "got $rc_fail — results from the passing pool may have bled into the failing pool"
fi
orch_shutdown "$pool_pass"
orch_shutdown "$pool_fail"
